Le Service de police de la Ville de Mont: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) still calls the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) to check the status of migrants, according to figures obtained by La Converse.
En 2023, le SPVM a passé 1 061 coups de: In 2023, the SPVM made 1,061 calls to the Agency for “status determination, warrant requests and previous removal orders,” according to a CBSA spokesperson in an email.
Si ce chiffre marque une claire diminuti: While this figure marks a clear decrease in calls compared with previous years, they nevertheless undermine trust among people without status in the metropolis, some experts believe.
Le service de police de la ville de Toro: The Toronto police service surpassed Montréal's for checks in 2023. But that has not always been the case. The Ontario metropolis contacted the CBSA 1,330 times in 2023, while the Vancouver police service called the agency only 552 times.
« À Montréal, ce chiffre tournait autour: “In Montréal, that number was around 3,500 calls a year in previous years,” says Caroline Labelle, an SPVM spokesperson.
Si cela représente un pas dans la bonne: While this represents a step in the right direction toward including people without status in municipal life, the collaboration between the police and the federal agency, which has the power to order deportations or detentions, should be ended entirely, according to a Concordia University professor.
« La première chose à faire, ce serait d: “The first thing to do would be to stop the collaboration between the municipal government and the CBSA. Yes, there is an improvement [because there are fewer calls], but the collaboration still exists,” laments Ted Rutland, a professor in the Department of Geography, Planning and Environment.
Les policiers ont quatre raisons d’appel: Police officers have four reasons to call the Canada Border Services Agency to check a person's immigration status.
D’abord, dans le cadre d’une enquête qua: First, as part of an investigation when another person's safety is at stake. Second, for driver's licence and vehicle registration checks. Third, for an investigation into criminal offences in which the person arrested is subject to an arrest warrant. And finally, as part of a warrant-based investigation.
Cette collaboration avec l’ASFC devient: This collaboration with the CBSA is becoming something of a “blind spot for the police,” believes Louis-Philippe Jannard, one of the coordinators at the Table de concertation des organismes au service des personnes réfugiées et immigrantes (TCRI). His doctoral research, in fact, focused on the detention practices of CBSA officers.
« Lors de l’une de mes entrevues avec un: “In one of my interviews with an officer, I was told that the SPVM was even a main partner,” he recounts.
Le fait que les migrants savent que des: The fact that migrants know checks can be carried out, even on flimsy pretexts, “undermines their mission to protect the public. Think of a case where a person is injured and needs an ambulance. Will a first responder check the person's identity? No, but that person without status might hesitate to dial 911 for fear that their identity will be looked up.”
Une autre inquiétude ? La détention dans: Another concern? Detention in an immigration holding centre. One of them is in Laval. People without status who are considered a risk by the Canada Border Services Agency, whose identity cannot be confirmed, or who are awaiting deportation but are feared unlikely to show up for their removal, can be held there.
« Ce qui est sûr c’est que, si la person: “What is certain is that if the person is subject to a removal order, it can lead to deportation. If the person has no status and has been in Canada for a while and is not complying with the removal order, I imagine the Agency uses it to lead to detention [at the Laval centre],” explains Mr. Jannard.
De son côté, Ted Rutland ajoute que, au-: For his part, Ted Rutland adds that beyond the fear caused by a status check, there is the plain fear of being arrested for trivial reasons.
« Nous savons que le service de police a: “We know that the police service stops racialized people much more often for traffic checks, for example. If those racialized people are also people without status, the risk is even higher for them,” laments the professor.
Il cite un rapport rédigé l’an dernier q: He cites a report written last year that analyzes the overrepresentation of racialized people in police stops. According to the document, Black people were 3.5 times more likely to be stopped than white people and 2.6 times more likely than people of Arab origin.
Le concept de « ville sanctuaire » est n: The concept of a “sanctuary city” was born in 1979 in Los Angeles, in the United States. It became increasingly popular in the 1980s and 1990s south of the border, as many refugees from Guatemala and El Salvador were fleeing violence in their countries.
La politique d’une « ville sanctuaire »,: The policy of a “sanctuary city,” although it is not officially defined anywhere, is not to ask residents for proof of citizenship and not to report them to border officers if they are undocumented.
« Une ville sanctuaire signifie essentie: “A sanctuary city essentially means that if you live in our city, you are our neighbour, you are part of our community, no matter what the federal government does. So the municipality will not concern itself with your immigration status; it will treat you like a citizen,” explains Mr. Rutland.
Il faut ici remonter à 2017, année où l’: Here we have to go back to 2017, the year former U.S. president Donald Trump closed the door to nationals of seven predominantly Muslim countries under an executive order – commonly known as the “Muslim Ban.” Nationals of Iraq, Iran, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen, Libya and Syria were then barred from entering the United States.
C’est dans ce contexte que l’ex-maire mo: It was in this context that former Montréal mayor Denis Coderre declared that Montréal was a “sanctuary city.” According to several people, this was only symbolic.
« Le fait qu’il y ait encore des appels: “The fact that there are still calls [from the SPVM to the CBSA] calls into question Montréal's label as a sanctuary city. We can't claim that Montréal is a sanctuary city,” insists Mr. Jannard during our phone call.
« En collaboration avec les partenaires: “In collaboration with partners in the health, social services and community networks, police officers direct undocumented people to resources that will help them, depending on their situation,” says the SPVM spokesperson.
